pr_body:
When creating snapshots in HDFS repository, there was no way to choose a specific HDFS replication factor.
Setting `hdfs.dfs.replication` to any number is ignored on the client side in `FileContext` API.

Here's an excerpt from [FileContext.create documentation](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/current/api/org/apache/hadoop/fs/FileContext.html#create-org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path-java.util.EnumSet-org.apache.hadoop.fs.Options.CreateOpts...-):

> The defaults for the following are SS [server-side] defaults of the file server implementing the target path.
> BufferSize - buffersize used in FSDataOutputStream
> Blocksize - block size for file blocks
> ReplicationFactor - replication for blocks
> ChecksumParam - Checksum parameters. server default is used if not specified.



HDFS allows setting a custom replication level when creating new files, but it has to be done via an argument.
This PR adds a new setting to HDFS repositories, `replication_factor`, which is then used whenever a file is created.
The default behavior is the same as it used to be - use HDFS cluster default.

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/90952 - I think the description there isn't accurate, as the setting is applied, it's just that this specific setting isn't effective on the HDFS client side.

Example API request to create an HDFS repository with replication factor set to 1:

```
PUT /_snapshot/estest
{
  "type": "hdfs",
  "settings": {
    "uri": "hdfs://namenode:9000/",
    "path": "/estest",
    "readonly": false,
    "replication_factor": 1,
    "conf.dfs.client.use.datanode.hostname": true,
    "conf.dfs.datanode.use.datanode.hostname": true
  }
}
```

In our use-case, the default replication factor on HDFS is too high for the amount of data that we want to snapshot. We might run out of disk space. It also isn't critical data for us, since most of it can be reindexed from elsewhere. Therefore, we want to use a lower replication setting. Changing it after snapshot creation isn't as viable, since we might run out of disk space first.

review_comments: Thanks for adding the verification logic above, but if someone sets the dfs.replication.max higher than a short value, we'll still have an issue here - maybe we should add a third check above to make sure that the replicationFactor is between 0 and max short as a hard stop, regardless of the configured min and max?

Good point! I've added a check that the replication factor is >= 1 and <= max short.

HDFS client lib throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `Replication must be greater than 0` when it's below 1, but I suppose it's better to also check that ourselves so that we can give a better exception message.

If the replicationFactor is larger than a short, then this call will return -1. On one hand, it feels like a mistake to request more than 32 thousand replicas. On the other hand, if the user is being cheeky or careless, a -1 value doesn't blow up, but rather the client silently ignores it and uses the server default which can lead to confusion. A larger (smaller?) negative number doesn't get verified until it hits the namenode in a create request either. If the incoming value is bad, I think I'd rather the setting be rejected as early as possible instead.

In fact, given the default max replication factor is 512, maybe we should be bounds checking this property value before accepting it anyway. Maybe even against the `dfs.replication.max` and `dfs.replication.min` settings in the hadoop configuration? Then at least you have to set it wrong in two places?

Hmm, that error message seems to be tied to the verification logic in the `BlobStoreRepository` class. If it doesn't have a version of the repository yet when doing the verification, it creates it, but the creation is done inside of the try catch block that reports an error about not being able to write to a path. I think as long as you're doing the validation inside of the `createBlobstore` method, that is the right place. The ultimate error message is likely out of scope for this PR.
